**Finding: compliant (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

**What I checked.** I read every planner candidate (§§ 1.5, 2.1, 7.2, 7.3, 27.3) and then swept the whole document for the LD trigger vocabulary: "liquidated damages" (no hits), "penalty" (one hit, in our favour), "early termination fee", "termination for convenience", "cancellation charge", "shortfall", "accelerate / immediately due and payable", "shall pay", and every occurrence of "terminat". I also reviewed the full payment stack (§§ 7.1–7.5), term/renewal (§§ 8.1–8.3), termination and its effects (§§ 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2), warranty remedies (§ 19.4), liability (§§ 21.1–21.4), and audit (§§ 22.1–22.3).

**Why it is compliant.**
- No Customer-payable liquidated sum, penalty, or minimum fee on termination exists anywhere, which satisfies the preferred element outright.
- § 27.3 expressly lets us terminate "without penalty"; § 7.1 blocks unidentified minimum-use or similar charges; § 7.3 blocks interest on amounts ultimately not due; § 10.2 gives us refunds on exit rather than an exit charge.
- § 22.2 (audit costs plus undisputed shortfall on a >5% underpayment) is recovery of amounts actually owed, not a liquidated or penal amount, so it is outside this rule.
- § 2.1's USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment is real exposure, but it is a minimum-commitment/exit-rights term reviewed under the minimum-commitment rule and is not cast as liquidated damages or an early-termination fee — I have not double-flagged it here.
- Service-credit references (§§ 1.5, 7.2 invoicing) run to our benefit and are compliant by design.

Since the clause set meets the preferred position, no upgrade drafting was needed and no redline was proposed.
